Simple Rustic Loaf

Served at: Palm Sunday · Maundy Thursday · Good Friday

1 round loaf (Serves 6-8)Prep 15 minutes (plus 12-18 hours rising time)Cook 45-50 minutes

This humble, rustic loaf, with its crisp crust and tender crumb, offers a comforting presence at your Holy Week table. It evokes the simplicity and solemnity of the Last Supper on Maundy Thursday and provides a grounding accompaniment for the reflective meals of Good Friday. Its straightforward preparation allows for quiet contemplation as you prepare for the sacred days ahead.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups (360g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon instant yeast
  • 1 1/2 cups (360ml) warm water (about 105-115°F / 40-46°C)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and instant yeast.
  2. Pour the warm water into the dry ingredients. Mix with a wooden spoon or spatula until a shaggy, sticky dough forms. Do not knead.
  3. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp kitchen towel. Let the dough rise at room temperature (around 70°F / 21°C) for 12 to 18 hours, or until it has doubled in size and is bubbly.
  4. Once risen, lightly flour a clean work surface. Gently scrape the dough out onto the floured surface. Fold the edges of the dough towards the center a few times to form a rough ball. Avoid overworking the dough.
  5. Place a piece of parchment paper (about 12 inches / 30 cm square) on the work surface. Carefully transfer the dough ball onto the center of the parchment paper.
  6. Cover the dough loosely with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rest for another 30 minutes while you preheat your oven.
  7. About 30 minutes before baking, place a 6-quart (5.7-liter) Dutch oven with its lid into your oven and preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
  8. Once the oven and Dutch oven are fully preheated, carefully remove the hot Dutch oven. Using the parchment paper as a sling, carefully lower the dough into the hot Dutch oven.
  9. Cover the Dutch oven with its lid and bake for 30 minutes.
  10. Remove the lid and continue to bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until the crust is deeply golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 200-210°F (93-99°C).
  11. Carefully remove the bread from the Dutch oven using the parchment paper and transfer it to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For a chewier crust, mist the dough with water before the uncovered baking step.
  • This bread is best enjoyed fresh, but leftovers can be stored at room temperature in an airtight container for up to 3 days or frozen for longer.
  • Experiment with adding a tablespoon of dried herbs (like rosemary or thyme) or a sprinkle of garlic powder to the dry ingredients for a subtly flavored loaf.
